evaluation: expanding-window rolling-origin with matured-label purge; the last chronological origin is the primary holdout. Training at origin t only uses examples whose label window closed at or before t. With holdouts=K the last K origins are reported as sequential holdout windows; their test rows are disjoint (one origin each) while their 12-month label windows overlap.

purge.rule: A training example may only be used at origin t when its label window has matured: cutoff + horizon_months <= t. Otherwise the label encodes events inside (t, t+horizon], i.e. the test window.
purge.description: Purged/embargoed rolling origin. The league result below is the purged one; the old overlapping-label variant is reported separately under leaky_labels_diagnostic.

holdout_origin_rule: The last K origins that have at least one purged training example. With quarterly origins and a 12-month horizon the first four origins have no matured training examples, so this equals the last K chronological origins.
constraints: Identical rows, algorithm and hyperparameters across ablations.
Training labels must mature before the evaluation origin (purge/embargo); the unpurged variant is diagnostic only.
Current-snapshot procurement is excluded from historical gain claims.
Consolidated company revenue is not product- or segment-level device sales.
Multi-window holdouts are separate origins, so their test rows never overlap; their label windows do.

constant_training_prevalence.description: Same probability for every holdout row: positive rate over eligible training origins.

company_base_rate.description: Positive rate of the company over eligible training origins; training prevalence for unseen companies.

track_base_rate.description: Positive rate of the technology track over eligible training origins; training prevalence for unseen tracks.

pair_base_rate.description: Positive rate of the exact company-track pair over eligible training origins; training prevalence for pairs without matured history. This one-parameter persistence benchmark is the honest comparator for the headline PR-AUC.

holdout_window_summary.rule: Per-window metrics are computed at each origin; mean/std/min/max aggregate the holdouts=K windows. std is the population standard deviation across windows, not a confidence interval.

financial_marginal_value.interpretation: Positive PR-AUC/Precision@K and negative Brier/ECE are improvements; one holdout is not proof of a stable causal effect.

baselines.lead_times: Same target lead times as the model metrics, so only the probability columns differ.

model_vs_pair_baseline.comparison: Paired bootstrap (rows resampled with replacement, identical rows for both predictors) of PR-AUC(model) - PR-AUC(pair_base_rate) on the untouched holdout, repeated for every holdout window.
model_vs_pair_baseline.interpretation: If the interval includes zero, the R&D features add no statistically detectable ranking value beyond stable per-pair activity persistence on that holdout window. A per-pair base rate is degenerate when most holdout pairs have no matured training history (never-observed entry candidates), in which case it collapses towards constant training prevalence.

leaky_labels_diagnostic.warning: NOT the headline result. Training rows here may have label windows overlapping the test window (up to horizon_months-3 months of overlap). Reported only to quantify the optimism of the previously published numbers.
leaky_labels_diagnostic.interpretation: deltas are purged minus leaky: positive PR-AUC means the purged model ranks better, positive Brier/ECE/FPR means the leaky numbers were optimistic (lower is better).

leakage_audit.limitations: As-of replay/consistency audit, not a proof of absence of semantic leakage: unversioned current product-code mappings, company aliases or target-definition choices applied to history cannot be detected this way. It also cannot re-verify provenance of dates themselves.
